identity.title: Document the governed execution boundary and external surfaces

human_pressure.one_screen_brief: Freeze the product and engineering boundary before adding scope-aware behavior. Define Governed Execution, opaque scope_ref, four external boundary surfaces, temporal attribution invariants, and an ownership matrix that keeps IAM, gateways, orchestration, retries, model routing, and producer-specific execution concepts outside Ailuros core.
human_pressure.why_now: The EverRun dogfood proved that run-wide semantics are too coarse. A stable producer-neutral contract is required before code changes.
do_not_misread: This pack is documentation-first and must not implement execution behavior.
scope_ref is opaque and producer-neutral; do not add pack_id, iteration_id, node_id, task_id, planner, coder, or judge to core contracts.
Do not turn future decision egress into an HTTP API in this pack.
red_lines: No runtime-specific vocabulary in canonical core semantics.
No IAM, RBAC, auth, session, workflow, retry, model-routing, or gateway ownership added to Ailuros.

machine_core.goal: Create a precise documented contract for Ailuros governed execution boundaries and the external ingress/egress surfaces that later packs must implement.
red_lines: No speculative policy DSL or platform API.
Do not weaken existing governance-boundary red lines.
invariants: Ailuros governs execution facts, constraints, decisions, provenance, and outcomes but does not own execution scheduling or action execution.
scope_ref is optional, opaque, stable, and producer-neutral.
Unknown or malformed evidence must never become implicitly clean, allowed, approved, or authorized.
Later governance context must not silently rewrite earlier attribution.
Decision and governed-outcome outputs remain evidence-backed and framework-neutral.

producer.artifact: current governance-boundary docs plus EverRun dogfood findings

observable_effect.assertion: The repository contains one canonical boundary contract that precisely states ownership, non-ownership, scope_ref semantics, external boundary surfaces, and temporal invariants.

proofs.assertion: Docs are internally consistent with ADR-0005 and roadmap boundaries and contain no producer-specific core model.

failure_semantics: Ambiguous ownership means the pack remains todo.
Any doc statement that implies Ailuros owns IAM, orchestration, retries, routing, or producer-specific execution concepts is a boundary violation.

steps.title: Define Governed Execution
details: Define run as a container and scope_ref as the optional finer-grained governance subject reference.
State that producer vocabulary stays outside canonical semantics.

steps.title: Define external surfaces
details: Document evidence ingress, governance-context ingress, governance-decision egress, and governed-outcome/audit egress.
Add a product ownership matrix for IAM, gateway, runtime, approval, budget, and Ailuros responsibilities.

steps.title: Define temporal invariants
details: Document attribution rules for policy snapshots, authority, approval, budget, and evidence over time.
Require unknown preservation and prohibit retroactive context rewriting.

steps.title: Align existing boundary doc
details: Update governance-boundary.md to reference the new scope contract and preserve ADR-0005 boundaries.

acceptance: scope_ref semantics are explicit and producer-neutral.
Four external surfaces and ownership matrix are documented.
Temporal governance attribution invariants are explicit.

must_check: No source or test files changed.
The docs clearly distinguish opaque references from IAM/auth/session semantics.
The docs keep execution scheduling, retry, fallback, model routing, and workflow execution outside Ailuros.
scope_ref is not coupled to EverRun, LangGraph, CrewAI, or any runtime vocabulary.
reject_if: Any producer-specific core field is proposed as canonical.
Ailuros is assigned ownership of IAM, auth, sessions, orchestration, retry, model routing, or workflow execution.
Unknown evidence is described as implicitly allowed or clean.

validation_notes.targeted_contract_coverage: Documentation and core-boundary tests are sufficient because this pack intentionally changes no runtime behavior.
